newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end up at six-year high.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end up at six-year high.

text.p: Taiwan share prices ended slightly higher on Saturday at a six-year closing high amid heavy profit-taking pressure, brokers said.
The index ended up 7.53 points or 0.09 percent at 8,661.72, off an intraday high of 8,744.17.
The close, a sixth straight day of gains, surpassed a 8,655.82 finish of April 9 to mark the index's highest close since 8,922.67 on May 9, 1990.
Turnover was a brisk T$137.3 billion in the shorter Saturday session.
"Sentiment is still quite bullish as the government so far had not made negative moves on recent stock market rebounds," said National Securities analyst Oliver Fang.
"But short-term profit-taking is inevitable especially when the index faces tough resistance at around 8,700," he said.
Car and retail shares rose most.
Textiles were also strong, with giant Hualon up by the daily seven percent limit to T$32.7 on hope that its Malaysian subsidiary may soon be listed in Malaysia's stock market, Fang said.
Financials rose, but foods, constructions and plastics fell.
Electronics stocks, the most active sector in recent trading, were mixed, with computer giant Acer up T$1.5 to T$74.5 but chipmaker United Microelectronics was down 50 cents to T$68.
For next week, a volatile 8,500-8,900 range was seen.
